runs.label: 中心化 · 7
runs.winner_manager_direction: Your multi-horizon momentum + reversal overlay with inverse-vol sizing had the worst Sharpe of all four variants (~-0.7 in both train and validation), suggesting the momentum signal is systematically the wrong sign in this universe/period. This is valuable evidence: rather than tuning parameters, first establish the SIGN and regime dependence of momentum here. Test a pure 60-day or 120-day momentum long-short at low turnover to confirm whether momentum is genuinely negative in-sample, and if so, consider FLIPPING the signal (short-term/long-horizon mean reversion at the index-relative level) or restricting momentum to long-only in high-dispersion regimes. Second, the momentum+reversal overlay may be cancelling itself; decompose it. Third, test whether a pure volatility-scaled trend/risk-parity style long-only exposure with market-neutral residualization changes the sign story. Keep gross<=1, cap 2%, dollar-neutral, report decomposition of returns by leg and by signal component.

runs.label: 中心化 · 17
runs.winner_manager_direction: Round 1 conditional low-vol/beta + reversal rotation lost on both periods (Sharpe -0.68/-1.13, max DD 0.50/0.36) despite lower turnover (~0.37), suggesting the long low-vol/short high-beta tilt was simply the wrong side of the market in this sample. Assignment: flip the investigation around and test the opposite conditioning. Instead of assuming the low-risk anomaly dominates, empirically check on train history whether high-beta/high-vol names outperformed (i.e., a positive high-minus-low beta spread) and in which regimes. Test a long high-momentum/high-beta versus short low-vol construction, and separately test a pure momentum quality tilt (long high 60-120 day return with low 20-day vol, short the mirror). Keep the market-trend (200-day MA) gate but let the data tell you whether risk-on should favor high-beta. Report which regime rule actually had positive gross performance, and propose a simpler version with explicit turnover control.

runs.label: 中心化 · 27（第3次）
runs.winner_manager_direction: Your point that the 2% cap forces 25+ names per leg is correct and confirms small concentrated books were always cap-bound, not gross-dangerous. Build the reusable construction layer as you proposed but benchmark it against a long-only equal-weight universe and against a long-short random-selection control to establish the sign of the cross-sectional return spread over 60 sessions. Test whether 60-session return-z has negative (reversal) or positive (momentum) edge and at what holding horizon it is cost-survivable. Also test net-long versions within the net tolerance plus a cash-like or low-vol long tilt, and report signal IC at 5-, 20- and 60-day forward horizons gross of costs so we can pick the horizon and sign with the best expected value before paying turnover.

runs.label: 混合 · 7
runs.winner_manager_direction: Your residual-reversal (beta-adjusted, inverse-vol weighted) had the highest turnover (~0.56) and negative Sharpe in both periods. Investigate: (a) the inverse-volatility weighting likely over-weights low-idio names; test equal-weight vs inverse-vol per side to see if the weighting choice flips the sign. (b) The market-vol gross scaling (0.12/mkt_vol) may invert risk timing — test constant gross vs vol-scaled. (c) Beta estimation over 60 days is noisy; test a simpler 1-day market-neutral residual (subtract cross-sectional mean return) vs beta-adjusted, and test 5-day vs 10-day residual horizon. (d) The edge may live in the underreaction of individual names to idiosyncratic news — test adding a volume-surprise or gap component to residual reversal. Prioritize turnover reduction since costs are large (~5bps and 0.42 total cost on train). Report which ingredient is robust across both train and validation.

runs.winner_manager_direction: You did not submit a strategy result this round. Independently develop and backtest a rule-based policy under the same constraints (single weight per ticker, |w|<=0.02, gross<=1, net~0, point-in-time only, no fitted models). Your assignment is diagnostic and complementary: focus on understanding why long/short cross-sectional signals are losing in this sample. Specifically (a) implement a simple long-only equal-weight eligible-basket benchmark and a long-only low-volatility tilt to establish what the unconditional drift and risk structure look like; (b) report approximate cross-sectional dispersion and the sign/scale of a generic 1-month reversal and 6-month momentum spread measured net of 5bps turnover cost; (c) determine whether the negative P&L seen by other workers is dominated by costs vs signal, by constructing a gross (pre-cost) proxy. Recommend one or two specific low-turnover, robust directions your diagnostics support.
